claims.text: The feedstock is pre-alloyed, gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder suitable for a standard powder-bed-fusion setup.
A secondary low-power laser scan is applied immediately after deposition of each layer to provide localized post-deposition annealing.
Operating the secondary laser at approximately 30–50% of the main laser power and at slower traverse speeds provides targeted tempering.
In-situ low-power laser annealing reduces residual thermal stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
In-situ low-power laser annealing refines microstructural features in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The intervention produces diminished thermal gradients and a refined distribution of grain sizes and precipitates.
Gentle reheating of just-solidified layers reduces the thermal gradients generated during rapid solidification.
Reducing thermal gradients permits stress relaxation and suppresses the formation of microstructural defects.
A more uniform microstructure with fewer internal stress concentrations improves both ductility and strength.
Annealed AlCrFeNiSi components will have lower residual stress than components made without in-situ thermal management under conventional high-thermal-load conditions.
Annealed AlCrFeNiSi components will exhibit higher strength and ductility than the conventional-process controls.
The intervention is most applicable to miniature components because their thermal mass permits rapid heat dissipation and manageable laser-induced heat accumulation.
Larger geometries may respond differently because they cool more slowly.
The optimal secondary-laser power and scanning parameters have not yet been established and require calibration.
The effect of the intervention on long-term fatigue resistance is not established.
